dedupe_keys.name: epa power plants and neighboring communities fossil power plants with emissions and socioeconomic indicators of nearby and downwind communities

description: The Power Plants and Neighboring Communities Mapping Tool and data from the US Environmental Protection Agency identify and characterise communities that may be exposed to air pollution from power plants. The map shows every power plant that burns fossil fuels, has generators of at least 1 MW nameplate capacity and supplies the grid, with plant size, fuel type, generation and annual SO2, NOx, CO2 and PM2.5 emissions, and links each plant to census block groups through three views: uniform 3-mile buffers, plant-specific buffers and long-range downwind areas. Socioeconomic indicators such as race and ethnicity, income, age, language and education come from the Census Bureau ACS 2018-2022 summary, and plant data from eGRID2022; a separate map shows recent and announced retirements of coal, gas and oil plants. Data are available online as free XLSX and CSV downloads for each view with a data dictionary, and the maps are ArcGIS Experience Builder dashboards on the EPA GeoPlatform. Licence (read on the provider page on 2026-09-28): Public domain (EPA web policy: EPA-produced data are in the public domain unless otherwise specified). Coverage is the United States. Caveats: the EPA notes that the tool does not evaluate air quality impacts or quantify health risk, and the plant data are for 2022. Simulation uses are linking generation assets to exposed populations for equity-aware retirement, siting and outage impact studies. Related records: data-epa-egrid-emissions-generation-resource-integrated-database is the plant data source.
